Recently, Ghana's GoldBod released a [report](https://goldbod.gov.gh/trade-reports/) of its trade with the Bank of Ghana. The report is a pdf document. Researchers interested in the data will have to find a way to extract the data. To solve that problem, we developed a Shiny web application specifically tailed for this report. Users simply upload the PDF and in return gets clean CSV ready to download. Here is how the interface looks like. 

Note: The app only runs locally due to pdftools package functionalities not available on static website like Github Pages. You will need to download the code from the [goldbod repository](https://github.com/TheoAnim/goldbod)

```{shinylive-r}
#| standalone: true
#| viewerHeight: 600
#| viewerWidth: 600
library(shiny)
library(pdftools)
library(stringr)
library(dplyr)
library(readr)
library(shiny)

ui <- fluidPage(
  titlePanel("GOLDBOD/BOG Trade Report Data Extractor"),
  
  sidebarLayout(
    sidebarPanel(
      fileInput("pdf_file", "Upload BoG Trade PDF", accept = ".pdf"),
      downloadButton("download_csv", "Download CSV")
    ),
    
    mainPanel(
      tableOutput("pdf_table")
    )
  )
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  
  pdf_data <- reactive({
    req(input$pdf_file)
    
    # Read text from PDF
    pdf_text_all <- pdf_text(input$pdf_file$datapath)
    lines <- unlist(lapply(pdf_text_all, function(p) strsplit(p, "\n")[[1]]))
    
    # Keep lines that look like table rows
    table_lines <- lines[
      str_detect(lines, "^[A-Za-z0-9]") & 
      str_count(lines, "[0-9]{1,2}-[A-Za-z]{3}-[0-9]{2}") >= 1 &
      str_count(lines, "[0-9]") >= 2
    ]
    
    # Function to parse each table line
    parse_line <- function(line) {
      items <- str_split(str_squish(line), "\\s+")[[1]]
      
      # Detect date positions
      date_idx <- which(str_detect(items, "^[0-9]{1,2}-[A-Za-z]{3}-[0-9]{2}$"))
      
      invoice <- items[1]
      date_inflow <- if (length(date_idx) >= 1) items[date_idx[1]] else NA
      date_supply <- if (length(date_idx) >= 2) items[date_idx[2]] else NA
      
      # Remove invoice + dates to isolate numeric columns
      numeric_part <- items[-c(1, date_idx)]
      
      # Parse numbers: handle commas, parentheses (negative), etc.
      numeric_clean <- sapply(numeric_part, function(x) {
        x2 <- str_replace_all(x, ",", "")
        x2 <- str_replace(x2, "\\(", "-")
        x2 <- str_replace(x2, "\\)", "")
        suppressWarnings(as.numeric(x2))
      })
      
      # Map numeric columns according to your official layout
      inflow_from_bog        <- if (length(numeric_clean) >= 1) numeric_clean[1] else NA
      expected_amount_supply <- if (length(numeric_clean) >= 2) numeric_clean[2] else NA
      actual_amount_supplied <- if (length(numeric_clean) >= 3) numeric_clean[3] else NA
      actual_volume_supplied <- if (length(numeric_clean) >= 4) numeric_clean[4] else NA
      over_under_supply      <- if (length(numeric_clean) >= 5) numeric_clean[5] else NA
      total_charges          <- if (length(numeric_clean) >= 6) numeric_clean[6] else NA
      
      return(c(invoice,
               date_inflow,
               inflow_from_bog,
               expected_amount_supply,
               actual_amount_supplied,
               actual_volume_supplied,
               date_supply,
               over_under_supply,
               total_charges))
    }
    
    # Parse all lines
    table_data <- lapply(table_lines, parse_line)
    df <- as.data.frame(do.call(rbind, table_data), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
    
    # Apply column names
    colnames(df) <- c(
      "Invoice",
      "Date_Inflow",
      "Inflow_From_BOG",
      "Expected_Amount_to_Supply",
      "Actual_Amount_Supplied",
      "Actual_Volume_Supplied",
      "Date_Of_Supply",
      "Over_Under_Supply",
      "Total_Charges"
    )
    
    # Convert dates
    df$Date_Inflow <- as.Date(df$Date_Inflow, tryFormats = c("%d-%b-%y", "%d-%b-%Y"))
    df$Date_Of_Supply <- as.Date(df$Date_Of_Supply, tryFormats = c("%d-%b-%y", "%d-%b-%Y"))
    
    # Convert numeric columns
    num_cols <- c("Inflow_From_BOG", "Expected_Amount_to_Supply",
                  "Actual_Amount_Supplied", "Actual_Volume_Supplied",
                  "Over_Under_Supply", "Total_Charges")
    df[num_cols] <- lapply(df[num_cols], as.numeric)
    
    df
  })
  
  # Display table
  output$pdf_table <- renderTable({
    pdf_data()
  })
  
  # CSV download
  output$download_csv <- downloadHandler(
    filename = function() paste0("bog_trade_report_", Sys.Date(), ".csv"),
    content = function(file) write_csv(pdf_data(), file)
  )
}

shinyApp(ui, server)

```
